steps.why: The two names are only front and back, so the answer is anchored by saying which end each daughter came from before listing what it inherited.
common_mistakes: Writing that the proter is the posterior daughter. Proter is the FRONT one.
Writing that the proter builds a new mouth. It keeps the parent's cytostome and cytopharynx.
steps.memory_tip: Proter and 'prior' share the same root, meaning the one in front; the front daughter keeps the parent's mouth.
steps.margin_note: Say anterior, then say what it inherits. Two lines are enough.

steps.label: Opisthe
lines: The posterior daughter is called the opisthe.
It keeps the posterior contractile vacuole of
the parent and forms a new cytostome, a new
cytopharynx and the other missing organelles.
steps.why: The parent has only one mouth, so only one daughter can inherit it; the other has to build its own, and that is the real difference between the two.
common_mistakes: Writing that the opisthe gets no nucleus. Both daughters receive a macronucleus and a micronucleus.
Writing that both daughters build a new mouth. Only the opisthe does.
steps.memory_tip: Opistho- means behind, as in opisthosoma; the behind daughter builds its own mouth.
steps.margin_note: The second mark is the new mouth parts the opisthe has to form.

insider_note: Both marks are decided by one word each — anterior for the proter and posterior for the opisthe — so write those two words before anything else.
